title: Which pack of biscuits is cheaper?
description: Two packs of biscuits hold different amounts, so the board finds the price of one gram in each by dividing the price by the grams, then compares the two. Keeko's doubt is that the pack with the smaller price tag must be cheaper.
teaching_notes: One idea: to compare prices of different amounts, find the price of the same amount, here one gram, by dividing the price by the amount. Watch for students who compare the price tags and ignore the grams.

source: A 250 g pack of biscuits costs ₹40 and a 150 g pack costs ₹2
video_script.why: The child can divide a whole number by a whole number but has not used division to compare two prices.
video_script.substitution: Dividing the price by the grams gives the price of one gram, which can be compared directly.
video_script.anchor: a big pack of biscuits and a small pack of biscuits, each with a price tag and a weight
video_script.wrong_move: compares only the two price tags and ignores that the small pack holds fewer grams
video_script.payoff_line: The two hundred and fifty gram pack is cheaper

final_answer.value: The 250 g pack, at ₹0.16 per gram
final_answer.spoken: the two hundred and fifty gram pack

maths_rules: 0.16 < 0.18, so the 250 g pack is cheaper
250 - 150 = 100, so the small pack holds 100 g less
video_script.design: Two packs stay on the board all video. The working band shows the price of one gram built for each pack, then the two prices side by side. Keeko's doubt puts the two price tags beside the two weights.
open_questions: The book text has no solved example about two packs of biscuits; the video follows the worklist example.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a big pack and a small pack of biscuits, each with a weight and a price tag

marks.big: the big pack and its weight and price tag appear
marks.small: the small pack and its weight and price tag appear

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about two packs of biscuits.
<bookmark mark='big'/>The big pack holds two hundred and fifty grams and costs forty rupees.
<bookmark mark='small'/>The small pack holds one hundred and fifty grams and costs twenty seven rupees.
Which pack is cheaper?

beats.on_screen: the two packs hold still with a question mark between them; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one gram of biscuit from each pack sits on a scale beside an empty price tag; the words price of one gram = price ÷ grams

marks.amounts: the two packs sit side by side with their different weights
marks.gram: one gram from each pack moves onto the scale and the empty tags appear
marks.rule: the words price of one gram = price ÷ grams are written

narration: <bookmark mark='amounts'/>The two packs hold different amounts of biscuits.
<bookmark mark='gram'/>To compare fairly, we find the price of the same amount from each pack, one gram.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The price of one gram is the price divided by the number of grams.

beats.on_screen: Given: big pack 250 g for ₹40; small pack 150 g for ₹27

marks.given: the two weights and prices are written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the big pack is two hundred and fifty grams for forty rupees.
The small pack is one hundred and fifty grams for twenty seven rupees.

marks.find: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which pack is cheaper.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, big pack: price of 1 g = price ÷ grams = 40 ÷ 250 = 40/250 = 4/25 = 16/100 = 0.16

marks.why: the step title and the big pack are lit
marks.hund: 4/25 becomes 16/100 with times 4 on the top and the bottom
marks.gram: 0.16 is written beside the big pack

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step one, find the price of one gram in the big pack.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide forty by two hundred and fifty, because the price divided by the grams gives one gram.
<bookmark mark='simp'/>Forty over two hundred and fifty is four over twenty five.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by four to get sixteen over one hundred.
<bookmark mark='gram'/>One gram of the big pack costs zero point one six rupees.

marks.why: the step title and the small pack are lit
marks.hund: 9/50 becomes 18/100 with times 2 on the top and the bottom
marks.gram: 0.18 is written beside the small pack

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step two, find the price of one gram in the small pack.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide twenty seven by one hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='simp'/>Twenty seven over one hundred and fifty is nine over fifty.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by two to get eighteen over one hundred.
<bookmark mark='gram'/>One gram of the small pack costs zero point one eight rupees.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: compare the two prices of 1 g: 0.16 < 0.18

marks.cmp: the two prices of one gram move side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Step three, compare the two prices of one gram.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Sixteen hundredths is less than eighteen hundredths.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the 250 g pack is cheaper, ₹0.16 for 1 g against ₹0.18

marks.ans: the answer is boxed and the big pack glows
marks.price: the two prices of one gram are tied back to their packs

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The two hundred and fifty gram pack is cheaper.
<bookmark mark='price'/>It costs zero point one six rupees for one gram, against zero point one eight rupees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two packs
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the two price tags 40 and 27 side by side with a tick on the smaller; then the two weights 250 g and 150 g appear and the tick is crossed out

marks.doubt: the two price tags appear with a tick on the smaller one
marks.gram: the two weights appear and the difference of 100 g is shaded
marks.fix: the tick is crossed out and one gram from each pack is lit

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the small pack is cheaper, because twenty seven rupees is less than forty rupees.
<bookmark mark='gram'/>But the small pack also holds one hundred grams less.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A price tag alone does not tell us which pack is cheaper. We must compare the price of one gram from each pack.
